results.summary_before: This project implements a 16-bit non-linear feedback shift register with two selectable non-linear feedback functions for cryptographic pseudo-random number generation. The mode select input switches between a high algebraic degree function and a chaotic variant, with the 16-bit state output on dedicated and bidirectional pins. It is seeded with 0xACE1 and requires only a clock and reset to operate, making it self-contained for testing with a logic analyzer. The design is intended for cryptographic primitives and demonstrates programmable non-linear feedback.
results.summary: This project implements BRISQ, an approximate IEEE-754 single-precision inverse square root unit. It receives one 32-bit FP32 operand over an 8-bit byte-serial input bus, performs one Newton-Raphson refinement using a Quake-style integer seed, and returns a 32-bit FP32 result over an 8-bit byte-serial output bus. The datapath uses a truncated positive-magnitude FP32-style multiplier and a parametric subtractor, with a default precision of 11 high fraction bits, and is explicitly not a fully rounded IEEE-754 FPU. The design is verified with a self-checking cocotb RTL vector test and a sweep test, and requires no external hardware.

results.summary_before: This design checks whether an 8-bit input value is a Fibonacci number. It compares the input against the Fibonacci numbers that fit in 8 bits and sets an output high if a match is found. The design is purely combinational and requires no external hardware. It is tested with a cocotb testbench that applies known Fibonacci and non-Fibonacci values.
results.summary: This project implements a simple I2C master controller that transmits one byte to a fixed slave address (0x50). When the START input is asserted, it serially sends an 8-bit data value over SDA while generating SCL, and it produces START and STOP conditions. The BUSY output indicates an active transfer, and DONE and ACK status outputs are also provided. Testing involves applying reset, placing an 8-bit value on ui_in, asserting START, and observing SCL and SDA activity with an I2C slave device, logic analyzer, or oscilloscope.

The design has no documented inputs or control signals; it only provides eight output bits from the LFSR state. The project appears to be a minimal demonstration of an LFSR, but the lack of documentation limits its practical application.
results.summary: This project implements a programmable-length ring oscillator designed as a Physical Unclonable Function for hardware security. The inverter chain delay path can be dynamically configured using sel_mux_0, sel_mux_1, and n_inv, and the circuit oscillates at a device-specific frequency due to process variations in the GF180MCU process. An integrated control path monitors sample capture events and triggers telemetry when output is ready, with debug and valid outputs on the dedicated pins. Testing involves reset, challenge selection, enabling the oscillator, setting tx_ready to acquire data, and then disabling the oscillator to save power; an oscilloscope, logic analyzer, or PMOD-connected microcontroller/FPGA can be used for validation.

results.summary_before: This design counts continuously and broadcasts the counter value every second over 100Mbps Ethernet using an application-specific Ethernet type. It reuses the Teapot Ethernet accelerator wrapper and requires an external Ethernet PHY PMOD with a LAN8720A and a 50MHz oscillator. The design autonomously sends packets, and testing involves connecting it to a local network and monitoring the packets. The project humorously aims to count until the heat death of the universe.
results.summary: This project provides test structures for GF180MCU analog support, consisting of a couple of large current mirror loads. A reference current is input on iref, multiplied internally by about 50x, and drawn from a selected power rail via enable pins. Sense wires are routed out to measure both the voltage drop of the power rails and the voltage raise of the VGND rail. Testing requires providing a test current to iref, toggling the appropriate enable pin, and using a programmable current source and precision multimeter.

results.summary_before: Tiny FABulous FPGA is a small FPGA fabric with 64 LUT4+FF logic cells, configurable via a bitbang interface, and designed for use with Yosys and nextpnr. It provides 26 I/O buffers, global buffers, and a system reset, and can implement simple Tiny Tapeout designs directly. The bitstream is uploaded while reset is applied, and no external hardware is required. The design is notable for being a fully open-source FPGA fabric on a Tiny Tapeout tile.
results.summary: This project implements a 256x8 SRAM for testing, though only the top 128 entries are addressable. It has 6 address bits, 8 write data bits, and 8 read data bits, with a gwen signal that must be de-asserted to write and otherwise puts the SRAM in read mode. The SRAM is entirely cleared on reset, and incoming data, write enable, and address are flopped once before the SRAM, with outgoing data flopped once before reaching the uo_out pins. No external hardware is required, and testing follows the pin functions described above.
